title: Explain a result to a classmate
objective: Use two numbers to explain a result and answer a question.

slides.title: Read the class counts
body: Practice data: students counted birds for ten minutes per place.
Pond: 12 birds. Garden: 8 birds. Field: 4 birds.
Point to a place. Say its name, its count and the count time.

slides.title: Hear a short conversation
body: A: Hello. Could you tell me about the garden?
B: We saw eight birds in ten minutes.
A: Did you see more there than in the field?
B: Yes. We saw four birds in the field.
A: Thank you. That helps.

slides.title: Take two roles
body: Bird counts in ten minutes: pond 12, garden 8, field 4.
A: You help teach the class. Greet B and ask about the pond.
B: Compare the pond and field. Use the two counts.
A: Check one number. Then ask about a different place.
B: Answer and close the conversation politely.

slides.title: Swap roles and try again
body: Practice counts: pond 7, garden 9, field 3 birds.
Use the same ten-minute count time.
New helper: Ask about the garden and field.
Listen for both counts. Ask again if one is unclear.

slides.title: Give useful feedback
body: Say one thing your partner did clearly. Give an example.
I understood the comparison when you said ___.
Choose one sentence to make clearer. Say it to your partner.
